title: The Six Stages of AI Adoption: a model built around identity, not tooling
description: A model for AI adoption that sorts people by internal experience rather than by tools deployed. Six stages — Nomad, Observer, Dabbler, Integrator, Architect, Innovator — each defined by a characteristic feeling and the question underneath it. The model's central practitioner claim is that some adoption stalls are better explained by identity, confidence, and self-permission than by skill gaps alone, most visibly in the transition from Integrator to Architect. Practitioner-built and useful for reflection, facilitation, and adoption design; it is not a validated psychometric instrument.
